text:
Anaheim arrives in New Jersey on a bad run: the Ducks are winless in four (0-4-0) after a 3-2 loss at the Islanders two days ago, and they are without Ryan Poehling, who is on injured reserve. Leo Carlsson has moved onto the wing beside Nesterenko and Killorn, and Nikita Klepov is up to 15:10 a night. The Devils, 3-2-0 in their last five, beat Colorado 4-3 at home on Tuesday and are better than their record, having controlled 58% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) while finishing and goaltending have cost them.

The five-on-five gap is wide. New Jersey has taken 61% of the expected goals in its games, Anaheim 43%. The Ducks also take 4.2 penalties a game, which keeps giving opponents power plays, and the Devils have the stronger penalty kill. In net, projected starters Lukas Dostal (ANA) and Nico Daws (NJD) are both in the picture. Dostal is at +2.9 goals saved above expected this season, Daws at -2.7 over three games, and Daws is in for Jake Allen.

Worth watching: Jack Hughes, who the model has at 37% to score and 73% for a point, and Cutter Gauthier, 34% to score on Anaheim's top power play. Ice Sheet's under-the-radar pick is Timo Meier, a third-liner whose shots have been dangerous: 3.1 expected goals in his last nine games, with Anaheim allowing the fourth-most per 60. He is 24% to score.
